prompt: Apply the four actions framework (Eliminate, Reduce, Raise, Create) to Nintendo's Wii.
modelAnswer: Eliminate: the race for graphics power and high-definition processing, complex controllers with many buttons. Reduce: technical specifications and production costs, game complexity and learning costs for new players, price of the console. Raise: fun, social and family play, accessibility for non-gamers (elderly, families). Create: motion control with the Wiimote, physical activity and party games (Wii Sports, Wii Fit). Result: a new market space of casual and family gamers (noncustomers of Sony and Microsoft) with lower costs and high value – value innovation rather than technological competition.
keyPoints: Link to noncustomers and lower costs (value innovation)

prompt: What are strategic groups, how are they identified, and why are they useful for strategic analysis?
modelAnswer: Strategic groups are sets of organizations in an industry that share similar strategic characteristics. They are identified along two types of dimensions: scope of activities (product range, geography, number of segments, distribution channels) and resource commitment (branding and marketing effort, vertical integration, quality, R&D, size) – e.g. supermarkets, convenience stores and corner shops in grocery retail. They are useful because (1) they show with whom a firm actually competes and on which dimensions – rivalry is most intense within groups; (2) they reveal unoccupied spaces that may be white spaces or black holes; (3) they highlight mobility barriers that protect a group and limit moves between groups.
keyPoints: Scope and resource-commitment dimensions with examples
Uses: real competitors, white spaces/black holes, mobility barriers

prompt: Present the six red-ocean traps identified by Kim & Mauborgne.
modelAnswer: 1) Making existing customers happier – instead focus on noncustomers. 2) Treating market-creating strategies as niche strategies – market creation de-segments markets. 3) Confusing technology innovation with market creation – value innovation matters. 4) Equating creative destruction with market creation – new markets need not destroy existing ones. 5) Equating market creation with differentiation – it also requires lower costs and prices. 6) Equating market creation with low-cost strategies – it also requires differentiation.
keyPoints: Not only differentiation / not only low cost
